title: Nsight photon trace: SM utilization sweep (Apr 2026)
summary: Quick notes from a focused Nsight sweep using a custom lightweight tracer (photon) to capture short-lived kernel chains under CUDA Graph replay. Goal: map SM active cycles vs kernel chaining patterns for decoder-heavy workloads and identify where occupancy appears artificially low despite high SM activity.
background: Motivation: customers hit occasional tail latency spikes on long-decoding sessions. Hypothesis is intermittent kernel starvation due to uneven microbatch scheduling + kernel-chaining that fragments SM allocation windows. Prior traces hinted at high SM clock but low active_warp_fraction in short windows. This run uses a high-sample-rate trace to capture sub-1ms gaps.
environment_setup: Cluster: ded-gpu-pool-us-west2-b, node type: A100-80GB (PCIE), driver 525.116, cuda 12.2. Container: rwinf/runtime:v3.7. Model: rw-instruct-13B-qat (decoder-only), seq_len=2048, kv-cache warm. Serving config: microbatch=1, dynamic_batcher disabled, cuda_graphs enabled for decode loop, stream priority default. Metrics hooks: nvtx + photon tracer + Nsight timeline capture (sampling 2us).
trace_runs: run-2026-04-12-10:01 - throttle test: artificially insert 0.5ms CPU jitter before kernel launch
run-2026-04-12-14:20 - chained-fuse: attempt kernel fusion flag on, replay-mode=streamed
run-2026-04-13-08:45 - prefetch-disabled: async-copy prefetching turned off to test hostcopy interference
observations: Baseline trace shows repeated short quiet zones ~150-400us between kernel launches despite CUDA Graph replay — visible as gaps in nvtx metadata and reflected in a drop of active_warp_fraction to ~0.12 for those windows.
SM_clock remains at ~100% but occupancy metric (resident warps per SM) is moderate (0.45) — suggests warps are resident but not issuing instructions continuously.
Throttled-run with CPU jitter exaggerated gaps and increased tail latency 95p -> +28ms. Gaps align with kernel enqueue time on host thread (single enqueue path becomes a serialization point).
No-graph run had higher overall latency and lower per-token variance but removed the micro-gaps. Dynamic_batcher introduced batching delay but smoothed occupancy.

Chained-fuse attempt reduced number of kernel launches per decode iteration by ~18% but increased per-kernel execution time; this shifted occupancy profile to longer active windows and removed the short idle dips.
Prefetch-disabled run exposed increased copy stalls; async prefetch overlaps were helping hide small kernel enqueue latencies — turning it off made quiet windows more frequent.

Nsight flameview shows kernel launch latency jitter correlates with a mutex contention in the cqueue (serving runtime scheduler) around request-coalescer path — intermittent lock hold times of 50-300us.
Photon tracer timestamps show that CUDA graph instantiation path occasionally triggers a small host-side malloc/free that takes ~120us and blocks enqueue thread (rare but high impact).
hypotheses: Short idle windows are host-side serialization artifacts (enqueue path + occasional memory ops), not true GPU starvation; GPU remains resident but not issuing because work isn't enqueued.

CUDA Graph replay masks some high-latency host ops by concentrating launches, but also hides when small host-side stalls occur, turning them into high tail latencies when they coincide with critical enqueue path.
Kernel fusion reduces number of enqueues and therefore surface area for host jitter; effective when per-kernel critical section is low-overhead, but risks increasing single-kernel runtime variance.
Async-copy prefetching mitigates host enqueue peaks by overlapping host work with DMA; disabling it reveals the underlying enqueue jitter problem.
Lock contention in request coalescer is a plausible root cause; micro-optimizing lock granularity or switching to lock-free enqueue for the hot path could remove short gaps.
actions_and_next_steps: Instrument enqueue path: add lightweight counters and timestamps around malloc/free and lock acquisition in the coalescer (ticket: JIRA-RT-7421).
Prototype lockless ring for GPU-enqueue hot path (Markus) and run A/B against baseline with photon tracer to confirm gap reduction.
Try a hybrid strategy: preserve CUDA Graph replay for steady-state but fall back to streamed replay when enqueue jitter detected (experiment in github PR).
Add heap profiling in runtime to find sporadic host mallocs on critical path; consider preallocating graph scratch buffers.
Schedule follow-up Nsight capture after lockless ring prototype: focus on sub-ms windows and compare active_warp_fraction CDFs.
Add a metric hook in Console: short-gap-count per-minute (defined as windows where active_warp_fraction < 0.2 and duration between 100us and 1ms) to correlate with customer tail incidents.
conclusions: Preliminary conclusion: tail latency micro-gaps are dominated by host-side enqueue jitter and occasional heap ops. Kernel-level fusion and lock-path optimization both reduce the observed gaps. Next iteration should focus on removing host-side serialization rather than GPU-side scheduling changes.
notes: This doc is rough — saving a few raw Nsight timeline exports to drive ticket discussions. Timeline snippets are large; see linked artifacts and PR for traces. If we confirm lock contention, schedule a short runway to roll the lockless ring on dedicated clusters first.
